candidates.title: Cable Crunches: The CORRECT Way To Do Them (Most People Are Wrong)
candidates.description:
Cable crunches are an effective exercise to target the rectus abdominis, engaging the upper and middle portions of your six-pack muscles. To reap the full benefits, it's crucial to execute them with proper technique, ensuring full-range engagement and avoiding common mistakes that can turn this exercise into a waste of time.

Begin by attaching a rope handle to a high pulley, kneeling about an arm's length away to maintain constant tension. Focus on curling your chest toward your knees, not using your arms, and keeping your hips stable. Try variations like facing away from the machine or adding a diagonal crunch to engage the obliques. If you lack a cable machine, plate-weighted crunches are a great alternative.

candidates.title: Full Crunch Machine - Abs Exercise
candidates.description:
Full Crunch Machine - Abs Exercise

💪 Subscribe channel: https://www.youtube.com/c/mytrainingapp

(Starting Position)

Sit down on the machine and hook your feet under the rolls. Stabilize your position by keeping your back against the support pad and holding both handles. This is the starting position.

(First Movement)

Now, exhale as you use your abs to lower your torso while raising your legs. Bring your knees and elbows as close to each other as possible while contracting your abs at the end of the movement. 

(Second movement)

Hold the contraction for a moment, and then inhale as you slowly return to the starting position. 

Repeat the movements until you have finished all of your reps

Add this cable crunch exercise to your abs / core workout!

Cable Crunch

Exercise Data
Type: Strength
Main Muscle Worked: Abdominals 
Equipment: Cable 
Mechanics Type: Isolation
Level: Beginner
Sport: No
Force: Pull

Kneel below a high pulley that contains a rope attachment.
Grasp cable rope attachment and lower the rope until your hands are placed next to your face.
Flex your hips slightly and allow the weight to hyperextend the lower back. This will be your starting position.
With the hips stationary, flex the waist as you contract the abs so that the elbows travel towards the middle of the thighs. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position as you inhale. Tip: Make sure that you keep constant tension on the abs throughout the movement. Also, do not choose a weight so heavy that the lower back handles the brunt of the work.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Variations: You can perform this exercise with a handle instead so that you can concentrate on each side of the abs separately by performing the exercise to the side.
